title: model loading failed - breadcrumbs
body:
Quick scratchpad / breadcrumbs while debugging repeated model load failures on dedicated infra (g4dn-like). Mostly raw commands + error snippets + hypotheses.

Context:
- Model: open-llm/large-chat-v2 (example) converted to our internal format.
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated pool (4x A10G equivalent), running container image rwinf/infer:stable-2026-02.
- Symptoms: first token generation fails with a crash during model weight loading. Happens intermittently on worker restart; some hosts succeed, others fail with consistent stack traces.
- Hypothesis space: partial download, sharded checkpoint index mismatch, wrong checkpoint format (safetensors vs torch), state_dict key mismatch, GPU OOM while allocating metadata, mmap/file descriptor limits.

Commands tried (local / on node):
- Check file sizes + md5sums:
  $ ls -lh /mnt/models/large-chat-v2/
  total 1.2T
  -rw-r--r-- 1 root root  512G Feb 19 16:12 model-00001.safetensors
  -rw-r--r-- 1 root root  512G Feb 19 16:12 model-00002.safetensors
  -rw-r--r-- 1 root root  128G Feb 19 16:12 model-00003.safetensors
  -rw-r--r-- 1 root root  2.0K Feb 19 16:12 model-index.json

  $ md5sum -c checksums.md5  # checksums.md5 provided during snapshot
  model-00001.safetensors: OK
  model-00002.safetensors: OK
  model-00003.safetensors: FAILED  # mismatch for 00003 on node i-0abc123

- Re-download / verify snapshot (s3):
  $ aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/large-chat-v2/ /mnt/models/large-chat-v2 --recursive --no-progress
  -> re-run md5sums -> still failing for model-00003 on that host only.

- Check inode / disk / file system issues:
  $ dmesg | tail -n 50
  [ 1234.567890] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1p1): ext4_journal_check_start: Detected aborted journal
  -> suggests possible disk corruption. Disk SMART shows increased reallocated sectors on i-0abc123.

- Attempted load with safetensors loader locally (python):
  >>> from safetensors.torch import load_file
  >>> x = load_file('/mnt/models/large-chat-v2/model-00003.safetensors')
  Traceback (most recent call last):
  ValueError: header length mismatch: expected 2048, got 1984  # indicates truncated file / corrupted header

- Alternative: try torch.load fallback (shouldn't be .pt but trying):
  >>> import torch
  >>> torch.load('/mnt/models/large-chat-v2/model-00003.safetensors', map_location='cpu')
  RuntimeError: unknown file format

- Check model-index.json vs actual shards:
  $ cat model-index.json  (shortened)
  {"weight_map": {"transformer.wte.weight": "model-00001.safetensors", "lm_head.weight": "model-00003.safetensors"}}
  -> lm_head is on 00003 which MD5 failed. If lm_head truncated -> immediate failure at init when weights are validated.

- Tried loading same model on control host (i-0def456) where md5 OK: loads fine. So problem is host-specific (disk/network).

- Intermittent failure case: sometimes node shows different error: OOM during allocation when mapping all shards at once. Error:
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating tensor of shape [4096, 32768]
  -> observed during map_location='cuda' path. But switching to lazy mmap / loading to CPU then moving to CUDA reduced OOMs.

- Tests run:
  - Attempted aria2c multipart download (faster) -> produced identical checksums when succeeded.
  - Tried huggingface-cli snapshot-download -> produced same shard set.
  - Ran `sha256sum` on a good host and compared -> mismatch only on failing host.

Error snippets collected from worker logs:
- ValueError: header length mismatch: expected 2048, got 1984
- safetensors.rs: parse error: unexpected EOF
- RuntimeError: failed to open shard file '/mnt/models/large-chat-v2/model-00003.safetensors': No such device or address
- OSError: [Errno 5] Input/output error while reading '/mnt/models/large-chat-v2/model-00003.safetensors'

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Disk corruption on host i-0abc123 causing truncated shard file. Evidence: dmesg ext4 errors + SMART reallocated sectors + md5 mismatch.
2) Network/efs NFS related partial write during earlier snapshot sync -> some writes truncated. Evidence: only one host shows bad file despite same s3 snapshot pull attempts; maybe earlier sync used a shared NFS mount.
3) Checkpoint assembly bug: model-index.json points to wrong shard or file offset. Less likely because other hosts load same index fine.
4) safetensors lib version mismatch attempted to parse a newer header format -> header-length mismatch. Check installed safetensors version.
5) Race in startup where loader prefetch/parallel downloads clobbered file while another process wrote it -> partial file.

Immediate mitigation steps applied:
- Drained failing host from pool, replaced disk (i-0abc123 -> reprovisioned).
- Added pre-deploy md5 verification step to dedicated worker init (fail fast and mark disk bad).
- Fallback path: if safetensors header parse fails, try re-download from canonical s3 snapshot and re-verify; if still failing, mark shard as bad and fallback to another replica or node.

Longer-term follow-ups / TODOs:
- Add per-shard replica checks + automatic re-replication when mismatch detected.
- Improve loader to stream-verify header + fall back to CPU streaming instead of mmap all shards at once to reduce OOM risk.
- Instrumentation: record checksum of each shard at boot and emit metric to telemetry (model.load.shard_checksum{status=ok|fail}).
- Constrain concurrent downloads per node to avoid saturating network and partial writes.
- Audit safetensors / loaders across images: we should pin a minimum version that supports our header format and add CI test that loads one object from each major model we host.
- Add a one-line quick-check script put in /usr/local/bin/model-shard-check that runs md5sum on all shards and returns non-zero on mismatch.

Notes to self (playbook snippets):
- Quick re-sync from s3: aws s3 cp --recursive --no-progress s3://redwood-models/large-chat-v2/ /mnt/models/large-chat-v2 && md5sum -c checksums.md5
- If safetensors parse error: attempt `python -c "from safetensors.torch import load_file; load_file('...')"` to get clearer exception.
- To work around OOM on startup: set environment variable RW_MODEL_LAZY_LOAD=1 to enable streaming/cpu-first load path (temporary, default is eager mmap).
- Disk debugging: sudo smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 | egrep 'Reallocated_Sector_Ct|SMART overall-health'

Slack / ticket refs: JIRA-7842 (incident), Slack thread above, PR#1123 adds md5 check at init.

Bottom line: for this incident the immediate root cause appears to be host disk corruption (truncated shard file) with safetensors header parse surfacing the failure. Fixes: reprovision host, add md5 pre-check, and add loader fallbacks + telemetry.

Unresolved: confirm whether any previous runs wrote to a shared NFS that caused the corruption cross-host; follow up with infra to check snapshot pipeline and any earlier rsync jobs that touch /mnt/models.

-- Jordan
